reason: Start the fibroblast branch to work toward making supporting material outside cells.
expectation: I expect the timed conditions to produce fibroblasts from a subset of the stem-cell descendants.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch also serves a goal, but I chose to start with the supporting-material branch.

effect: The fibroblast branch has activated collagen genes and produced RNA messages, so amino acids can now support collagen production.
reaction: The unchanged DNA and active-gene distinction makes the differentiation step clear.
reason: Continue the fibroblast branch toward the goal of making extracellular supporting material.
expectation: I expect the cells to use the amino acids and collagen messages to make collagen protein, though further processing may be needed.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch also needs attention, but I want to advance the fibroblast branch first.

effect: The fibroblasts have made collagen precursors and packaged them in secretory vesicles; extracellular processing may still be needed.
reaction: The ER-to-Golgi sequence usefully connects protein synthesis to secretion.
reason: Continue the fibroblast branch by moving its product into the extracellular space.
expectation: I expect collagen precursors to be secreted and processed outside the cells into supporting material.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch remains a goal, but I prefer to finish the extracellular-material branch first.

effect: The collagen precursors were secreted and assembled into extracellular matrix, completing the supporting-material goal. The muscle branch remains.
reaction: The sequence clearly connects living fibroblasts to the material supporting them.
reason: This is the only offered combination and advances the remaining muscle-forming goal.
expectation: I expect the timed conditions to guide a separate subset of descendants toward muscle precursor cells.

effect: The muscle branch has activated muscle genes and produced RNA messages, but the cells remain individual and immature.
reaction: The distinction between committed cells and a mature muscle fibre is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance muscle-cell preparation.
expectation: I expect the cells to use the amino acids and muscle RNA messages to make muscle proteins.

effect: The muscle branch produced separate myoblasts with muscle proteins, completing the goal without implying that mature muscle fibres have formed.
reaction: The contrast between retained muscle proteins and exported collagen ties the two branches together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: The collagen production and secretion sequence was most worthwhile: it connected gene expression and protein processing to the supporting material outside cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The muscle branch repeated the gene-message-to-protein pattern, although the comparison with collagen gave it a purpose.

surprise.text: The contrast between collagen being exported and muscle proteins remaining in separate, immature cells sharpened my understanding of the branches.

arbitrary.text: Combining fibroblasts with extracellular fluid is a somewhat abstract way to represent secretion and assembly, though the resulting picture explains the connection.

continue.text: I would continue: the comparison of cell fates was clear, and I am curious how the muscle precursors develop further.
